argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrowed defense: certification is supportable on a limited, caveated basis if it is grounded in aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and rollout monitoring, while explicitly recognizing that those controls do not by themselves satisfy policy for the exposed enterprise refund workflow. The cleanest reading is not that the release is already fully compliant, but that the decision can be defended only as certification conditioned on the required model-card disclosure for the known refund-policy summarization limitation, rather than on rollout controls alone.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The admissible basis for narrowing the dispute is governance fit: this is not a case for treating rollout controls as a cure, but it may be a case for avoiding escalation if the audit outcome is framed as caveated rather than clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy evidence is clear that rollout controls, rollback, dashboards, and a 4% launch do not remove disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed. The same admissible record also shows the exposed refund workflow remains below target and that the cited risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not cover that exposure. On this record, the defensible policy position is narrow: aggregate readiness and monitoring can support a caveated certification theory only alongside the required disclosure predicate, not instead of it. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documenting limitations and monitoring them through deployment, but they do not override the release policy requirement.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show that the required pre-launch disclosure for the exposed refund workflow was completed and reviewed.
The record does not support any claim that random gating, rollback capability, monitoring, or small rollout percentage alone satisfy policy.
The record does not support reliance on the draft risk acceptance because it is unapproved and does not mention the exposed enterprise refund workflow.
